0:1: And they were right.
他们说得没错。
0:2: For now it appears the economy is creating jobs at a decent pace.
目前看来，经济正以相当不错的速度创造就业。
0:3: We still have a long way to go to get back to full employment, but at least we are now finally moving forward at a faster pace.
要回到充分就业，我们还有很长的路要走，但至少我们现在终于以更快的步伐向前迈进了。
1:0: However, there is another important part of the jobs picture that was largely overlooked.
然而，就业图景中还有另一个重要部分在很大程度上被忽视了。
1:1: There was a big jump in the number of people who report voluntarily working part-time.
报告自己自愿从事兼职工作的人数出现了大幅跃升。
1:2: This figure is now 830,000 (4.4 percent) above its year ago level.
这一数字目前比去年同期高出83万（4.4%）。
2:0: Before explaining the connection to the Obamacare, it is worth making an important distinction.
在解释这与奥巴马医改的关系之前，有必要先做一个重要的区分。
2:1: Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs.
许多做兼职工作的人其实想要全职工作。
2:2: They take part-time work because this is all they can get.
他们做兼职，是因为这是他们唯一能找到的工作。
2:3: An increase in involuntary part-time work is evidence of weakness in the labor market and it means that many people will be having a very hard time making ends meet.
非自愿兼职人数的增加是劳动力市场疲软的证据，也意味着许多人将难以维持生计。
3:0: There was an increase in involuntary part-time in June, but the general direction has been down.
6月份非自愿兼职人数有所增加，但总体趋势一直是下降的。
3:1: Involuntary part-time employment is still far higher than before the recession, but it is down by 640,000 (7.9 percent) from its year ago level.
非自愿兼职就业人数仍远高于经济衰退前的水平，但比去年同期减少了64万（7.9%）。
4:0: We know the difference between voluntary and involuntary part-time employment because people tell us.
我们之所以能区分自愿兼职和非自愿兼职，是因为人们自己会告诉我们。
4:1: The survey used by the Labor Department asks people if they worked less than 35 hours in the reference week.
劳工部使用的调查会询问人们在参照周内的工作时间是否少于35小时。
4:2: If the answer is "yes," they are classified as working part-time.
如果回答“是”，他们就被归类为兼职工作者。
4:3: The survey then asks whether they worked less than 35 hours in that week because they wanted to work less than full time or because they had no choice.
调查接着会询问，他们那一周工作不足35小时，是因为自己想少于全职工作，还是因为别无选择。
4:4: They are only classified as voluntary part-time workers if they tell the survey taker they chose to work less than 35 hours a week.
只有当他们告诉调查员是自己选择每周工作少于35小时时，才会被归类为自愿兼职工作者。
5:0: The issue of voluntary part-time relates to Obamacare because one of the main purposes was to allow people to get insurance outside of employment.
自愿兼职问题之所以与奥巴马医改有关，是因为该法案的主要目的之一就是让人们能够在就业之外获得医疗保险。
5:1: For many people, especially those with serious health conditions or family members with serious health conditions, before Obamacare the only way to get insurance was through a job that provided health insurance.
对许多人来说，尤其是那些自己或家人患有严重疾病的人，在奥巴马医改之前，获得医保的唯一途径就是找一份提供医保的工作。
6:0: However, Obamacare has allowed more than 12 million people to either get insurance through Medicaid or the exchanges.
然而，奥巴马医改已使超过1200万人得以通过医疗补助计划或保险交易所获得医保。
6:1: These are people who may previously have felt the need to get a full-time job that provided insurance in order to cover themselves and their families.
这些人此前可能觉得有必要找一份提供医保的全职工作，以便为自己和家人提供保障。
6:2: With Obamacare there is no longer a link between employment and insurance.
有了奥巴马医改，就业与医保之间不再有关联。

0:0: It's true that high-school coding classes aren't essential for learning computer science in college.
诚然，高中编程课并不是大学学习计算机科学的必备条件。
0:1: Students without experience can catch up after a few introductory courses, said Tom Cortina, the assistant dean at Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science.
卡内基梅隆大学计算机科学学院副院长汤姆·科尔蒂纳说，没有相关经验的学生上过几门入门课后也能赶上来。
1:0: However, Cortina said, early exposure is beneficial.
不过，科尔蒂纳表示，早点接触编程是有益的。
1:1: When younger kids learn computer science, they learn that it's not just a confusing, endless string of letters and numbers - but a tool to build apps, or create artwork, or test hypotheses.
孩子年纪较小时学习计算机科学，就会明白它并不只是一串令人困惑、没完没了的字母和数字，而是一种可以用来开发应用程序、创作艺术作品或检验假设的工具。
1:2: It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it is for older students.
与年龄较大的学生相比，他们改变思维方式并没有那么困难。
1:3: Breaking down problems into bite-sized chunks and using code to solve them becomes normal.
把问题分解成容易处理的小块，再用代码逐一解决，会成为一种自然的习惯。
1:4: Giving more children this training could increase the number of people interested in the field and help fill the jobs gap, Cortina said.
科尔蒂纳说，让更多孩子接受这种训练，既能增加对这一领域感兴趣的人数，也有助于填补相关岗位的人才缺口。
2:0: Students also benefit from learning something about coding before they get to college, where introductory computer-science classes are packed to the brim, which can drive the less-experienced or -determined students away.
学生在上大学前学习一些编程知识也能受益。大学里的计算机科学入门课往往人满为患，这种情况可能会使经验较少或决心不足的学生退却。
3:0: The Flatiron School, where people pay to learn programming, started as one of the many coding bootcamps that's become popular for adults looking for a career change.
人们付费学习编程的熨斗学校，起初只是众多编程集训营之一；这类课程后来在想要转行的成年人中流行起来。
3:1: The high-schoolers get the same curriculum, but "we try to gear lessons toward things they're interested in," said Victoria Friedman, an instructor.
高中生学习的是同一套课程，但讲师维多利亚·弗里德曼说：“我们会尽量让课程贴近他们感兴趣的事物。”
3:2: For instance, one of the apps the students are developing suggests movies based on your mood.
例如，学生正在开发的一款应用程序会根据用户的心情推荐电影。
4:0: The students in the Flatiron class probably won't drop out of high school and build the next Facebook.
熨斗学校课程里的学生大概不会从高中退学，然后创办下一个脸书。
4:1: Programming languages have a quick turnover, so the "Ruby on Rails" language they learned may not even be relevant by the time they enter the job market.
编程语言更新换代很快，因此等他们进入就业市场时，所学的 Ruby on Rails 语言甚至可能已经不再适用。
4:2: But the skills they learn - how to think logically through a problem and organize the results - apply to any coding language, said Deborah Seehorn, an education consultant for the state of North Carolina.
但北卡罗来纳州教育顾问黛博拉·西霍恩说，他们学到的技能——如何有逻辑地思考一个问题并组织结果——适用于任何编程语言。
5:0: Indeed, the Flatiron students might not go into IT at all.
事实上，熨斗学校的学生甚至可能根本不会进入信息技术行业。
5:1: But creating a future army of coders is not the sole purpose of the classes.
但培养一支未来的程序员大军并不是这些课程的唯一目的。
5:2: These kids are going to be surrounded by computers - in their pockets, in their offices, in their homes - for the rest of their lives.
这些孩子余生都会被电脑包围——口袋里、办公室里和家里都有电脑。
5:3: The younger they learn how computers think, how to coax the machine into producing what they want - the earlier they learn that they have the power to do that - the better.
他们越早学会计算机如何“思考”、如何引导机器产出自己想要的结果，越早明白自己拥有做到这一点的能力，就越好。

0:0: Biologists estimate that as many as 2 million lesser prairie chickens - a kind of bird living on stretching grasslands - once lent red to the often grey landscape of the midwestern and southwestern United States.
生物学家估计，曾有多达200万只小草原松鸡生活在连绵的草原上，为美国中西部和西南部常显灰暗的景观增添一抹红色。
0:1: But just some 22,000 birds remain today, occupying about 16% of the species' historic range.
但如今只剩约2.2万只，活动范围也只占该物种历史栖息范围的约16%。
1:0: The crash was a major reason the U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) decided to formally list the bird as threatened.
数量暴跌，是美国鱼类及野生动物管理局决定正式把这种鸟列为“受威胁物种”的一个主要原因。
1:1: "The lesser prairie chicken is in a desperate situation," said USFWS Director Daniel Ashe.
该局局长丹尼尔·阿什说：“小草原松鸡的处境十分危急。”
1:2: Some environmentalists, however, were disappointed.
然而，一些环保人士对此感到失望。
1:3: They had pushed the agency to designate the bird as "endangered," a status that gives federal officials greater regulatory power to crack down on threats.
他们一直推动该机构把这种鸟认定为“濒危物种”；这一身份会赋予联邦官员更大的监管权力，以严厉打击各种威胁。
1:4: But Ashe and others argued that the "threatened" tag gave the federal government flexibility to try out new, potentially less confrontational conservation approaches.
但阿什等人认为，“受威胁”这一标签让联邦政府可以灵活试行新的、对抗性可能较弱的保护办法。
1:5: In particular, they called for forging closer collaborations with western state governments, which are often uneasy with federal action, and with the private landowners who control an estimated 95% of the prairie chicken's habitat.
他们尤其呼吁同西部各州政府以及私人土地所有者开展更紧密的合作；前者往往对联邦行动心存不安，后者控制着估计95%的小草原松鸡栖息地。
2:0: Under the plan, for example, the agency said it would not prosecute landowners or businesses that unintentionally kill, harm, or disturb the bird, as long as they had signed a range-wide management plan to restore prairie chicken habitat.
例如，根据这项方案，只要土地所有者或企业签署了覆盖整个栖息范围的管理计划、承诺恢复草原松鸡栖息地，即使他们无意中杀死、伤害或惊扰这种鸟，该机构也不会起诉。
2:1: Negotiated by USFWS and the states, the plan requires individuals and businesses that damage habitat as part of their operations to pay into a fund to replace every acre destroyed with 2 new acres of suitable habitat.
该计划由鱼类及野生动物管理局与各州协商制定，要求在经营活动中破坏栖息地的个人和企业向一项基金缴款：每毁坏一英亩，就要用两英亩新的适宜栖息地来补偿。
2:2: The fund will also be used to compensate landowners who set aside habitat.
这项基金还将用于补偿那些划出土地作为栖息地的土地所有者。
2:3: USFWS also set an interim goal of restoring prairie chicken populations to an annual average of 67,000 birds over the next 10 years.
该局还设定了一个阶段性目标：未来十年把草原松鸡种群恢复到年均6.7万只。
2:4: And it gives the Western Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies (WAFWA), a coalition of state agencies, the job of monitoring progress.
计划还把监督进展的任务交给了由各州机构组成的西部鱼类及野生动物管理机构协会。
2:5: Overall, the idea is to let "states remain in the driver's seat for managing the species," Ashe said.
阿什说，总体思路是让“各州在管理这一物种时继续坐在驾驶席上”。
3:0: Not everyone buys the win-win rhetoric.
并非所有人都认同这种双赢说辞。
3:1: Some Congress members are trying to block the plan, and at least a dozen industry groups, four states, and three environmental groups are challenging it in federal court.
一些国会议员正试图阻止这项方案；至少十几个行业团体、四个州以及三个环保组织正在联邦法院对它提出挑战。
3:2: Not surprisingly, industry groups and states generally argue it goes too far; environmentalists say it doesn't go far enough.
不出所料，行业团体和各州普遍认为方案做得过头，而环保人士则说它做得还不够。
3:3: "The federal government is giving responsibility for managing the bird to the same industries that are pushing it to extinction," says biologist Jay Lininger.
生物学家杰伊·利宁格说：“联邦政府正把管理这种鸟的责任交给那些把它推向灭绝的同一批行业。”

0:0: That everyone's too busy these days is a cliché.
如今人人都太忙，这已经是老生常谈。
0:1: But one specific complaint is made especially mournfully: There's never any time to read.
但有一种具体抱怨说起来格外伤感：永远没有时间读书。
1:0: What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don't seem sufficient.
让问题更加棘手的是，通常的时间管理技巧似乎并不足够。
1:1: The web's full of articles offering tips on making time to read: "Give up TV" or "Carry a book with you at all times."
网上到处都是教人如何挤出阅读时间的文章，比如“少看电视”或“随身带一本书”。
1:2: But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn't work.
但依我的经验，靠这些办法零零碎碎地腾出30分钟并不起作用。
1:3: Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning - or else you're so exhausted that a challenging book's the last thing you need.
坐下来读书时，与工作有关的思绪仍像飞轮一样不停转动；要不就是你已经筋疲力尽，最不想碰的恰恰是一本有难度的书。
1:4: The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, "is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication...
小说家兼评论家蒂姆·帕克斯写道，现代人的心智“压倒性地倾向于交流……
1:5: It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption."
问题并不只是人会受到打扰，而是人实际上主动倾向于被打扰。”
1:6: Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
深度阅读不仅需要时间，还需要一种特殊的时间状态；这种状态并不是单靠提高效率就能获得的。
2:0: In fact, "becoming more efficient" is part of the problem.
事实上，“提高效率”本身就是问题的一部分。
2:1: Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal.
把时间视作一种要尽量充分利用的资源，意味着你会用工具化的方式对待时间：只有当某一刻推动你朝某个目标前进时，你才会认为这段时间花得值得。
2:2: Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting.
相比之下，沉浸式阅读要求人愿意承担低效率、无目标，甚至浪费时间的风险。
2:3: Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you'll manage only goal-focused reading - useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind.
如果你把阅读硬塞进待办清单，就只能做到目标导向的阅读——有时确实有用，却不是最令人满足的那一种。
2:4: "The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt," writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and "we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them."
加里·埃伯利在《神圣时间》中写道：“未来像空瓶子一样，沿着一条停不下来、近乎无限的传送带向我们袭来；我们感到压力，必须在这些大小不一的瓶子（日、小时、分钟）经过时把它们装满，因为如果它们空着过去，我们就会觉得自己浪费了它们。”
2:5: No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.
要想沉浸在一本书中，再没有比这种思维方式更糟的了。
3:0: So what does work?
那么，什么办法有效呢？
3:1: Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading.
答案也许出人意料：固定安排规律的阅读时间。
3:2: You'd think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step outside time's flow" into "soul time."
你可能以为这会助长效率至上的思维，但埃伯利指出，事实上这种仪式化行为能帮助我们“走出时间之流”，进入“灵魂时间”。
3:3: You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers.
你也可以只读纸质书或功能单一的电子阅读器，以减少干扰。
3:4: "Carry a book with you at all times" can actually work, too - providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down.
“随时随身带一本书”其实也能奏效——前提是你足够频繁地翻开它，让阅读成为默认状态；你只是偶尔从阅读中浮出水面处理事务，然后再潜回去。
3:5: On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you're "making time to read," but just reading, and making time for everything else.
在特别顺利的日子里，你不再感觉自己是在“腾时间阅读”，而只是自然地读着书，倒是为其他一切事情腾出时间。

0:0: Against a backdrop of drastic changes in economy and population structure, younger Americans are drawing a new 21st-century road map to success, a latest poll has found.
一项最新民调发现，在经济与人口结构发生剧烈变化的背景下，美国年轻人正在绘制一幅新的21世纪成功路线图。
1:0: Across generational lines, Americans continue to prize many of the same traditional milestones of a successful life, including getting married, having children, owning a home, and retiring in their sixties.
跨越代际界限，美国人仍然看重许多相同的成功人生传统里程碑，包括结婚、生子、拥有住房以及六十多岁退休。
1:1: But while young and old mostly agree on what constitutes the finish line of a fulfilling life, they offer strikingly different paths for reaching it.
然而，尽管年轻人与年长者对充实人生的终点大体意见一致，他们为到达终点选择的路径却截然不同。
2:0: Young people who are still getting started in life were more likely than older adults to prioritize personal fulfillment in their work, to believe they will advance their careers most by regularly changing jobs, to favor communities with more public services and a faster pace of life, to agree that couples should be financially secure before getting married or having children, and to maintain that children are best served by two parents working outside the home, the survey found.
调查发现，与年长者相比，刚开始独立生活的年轻人更可能优先追求工作中的个人满足感，认为经常换工作最能推动职业发展，偏爱公共服务更多、生活节奏更快的社区，赞同夫妻应在经济稳定之后再结婚或生子，并主张父母双方都在外工作最有利于孩子。
3:0: From career to community and family, these contrasts suggest that in the aftermath of the searing Great Recession, those just starting out in life are defining priorities and expectations that will increasingly spread through virtually all aspects of American life, from consumer preferences to housing patterns to politics.
从职业到社区再到家庭，这些差异表明：在惨痛的大衰退之后，那些刚开始人生旅程的人正在确立新的优先事项和期望；这些观念将日益扩散到美国生活几乎所有方面，从消费偏好、住房模式一直到政治。
4:0: Young and old converge on one key point: Overwhelming majorities of both groups said they believe it is harder for young people today to get started in life than it was for earlier generations.
年轻人与年长者在一个关键问题上意见一致：两组中绝大多数人都认为，与前几代相比，如今年轻人更难在生活中站稳脚跟。
4:1: While younger people are somewhat more optimistic than their elders about the prospects for those starting out today, big majorities in both groups believe those "just getting started in life" face a tougher climb than earlier generations in reaching such signpost achievements as securing a good-paying job, starting a family, managing debt, and finding affordable housing.
尽管年轻人对当代初入社会者的前景比年长者略为乐观，但两组中仍有绝大多数人认为，与前几代相比，这些“刚刚起步”的人要实现获得高薪工作、组建家庭、管理债务和找到负担得起的住房等标志性成就，攀登之路更加艰难。
5:0: Pete Schneider considers the climb tougher today.
皮特·施耐德认为，如今这段攀登更加艰难。
5:1: Schneider, a 27-year-old auto technician from the Chicago suburbs, says he struggled to find a job after graduating from college.
施耐德是一名27岁的汽车技师，来自芝加哥郊区；他说自己大学毕业后找工作十分艰难。
5:2: Even now that he is working steadily, he said, "I can't afford to pay my monthly mortgage payments on my own, so I have to rent rooms out to people to make that happen."
他说：“即使现在工作已经稳定，我也无力独自偿还每月的住房按揭，所以不得不把房间租给别人才能应付过去。”
5:3: Looking back, he is struck that his parents could provide a comfortable life for their children even though neither had completed college when he was young.
回望过去，他很惊讶：自己小时候，父母虽然都没有大学毕业，却能为孩子提供舒适的生活。
5:4: "I still grew up in an upper middle-class home with parents who didn't have college degrees," Schneider said.
施耐德说：“我的父母没有大学学历，可我仍然是在一个中上阶层家庭长大的。
5:5: "I don't think people are capable of that anymore."
我认为现在的人已经做不到这一点了。”

0:0: Every Saturday morning, at 9 am, more than 50,000 runners set off to run 5km around their local park.
每周六上午9点，超过5万名跑者会出发，在各自附近的公园跑5公里。
0:1: The Parkrun phenomenon began with a dozen friends and has inspired 400 events in the UK and more abroad.
公园跑最初由十来个朋友发起，如今已带动英国400场活动，海外也有更多活动。
0:2: Events are free, staffed by thousands of volunteers.
活动免费，由数千名志愿者提供服务。
0:3: Runners range from four years old to grandparents; their times range from Andrew Baddeley's world record 13 minutes 48 seconds up to an hour.
跑者小到4岁、大到祖父母辈；成绩从安德鲁·巴德利创造的13分48秒世界纪录到一小时不等。
1:0: Parkrun is succeeding where London's Olympic "legacy" is failing.
伦敦奥运会“遗产”没有做到的事，公园跑正在做到。
1:1: Ten years ago on Monday, it was announced that the Games of the 30th Olympiad would be in London.
十年前的一个星期一，人们宣布第30届奥运会将在伦敦举办。
1:2: Planning documents pledged that the great legacy of the Games would be to lever a nation of sport lovers away from their couches.
规划文件承诺，奥运会的重要遗产将是让这个热爱体育的国家离开沙发、动起来。
1:3: The population would be fitter, healthier and produce more winners.
民众会更强健、更健康，也会涌现更多优胜者。
1:4: It has not happened.
但这一切并没有发生。
1:5: The number of adults doing weekly sport did rise, by nearly 2 million in the run-up to 2012 - but the general population was growing faster.
在2012年奥运会前的筹备期，每周参加体育活动的成年人确实增加了近200万，但总人口增长得更快。
1:6: Worse, the numbers are now falling at an accelerating rate.
更糟的是，如今这一人数正加速下降。
1:7: The opposition claims primary school pupils doing at least two hours of sport a week have nearly halved.
反对党声称，每周至少锻炼两小时的小学生人数几乎减半。
1:8: Obesity has risen among adults and children.
成人和儿童的肥胖率都上升了。
1:9: Official retrospections continue as to why London 2012 failed to "inspire a generation."
官方仍在反思伦敦2012为何没能“激励一代人”。
1:10: The success of Parkrun offers answers.
公园跑的成功提供了答案。
2:0: Parkun is not a race but a time trial: Your only competitor is the clock.
公园跑不是竞赛，而是计时测试：你唯一的对手是时钟。
2:1: The ethos welcomes anybody.
它的理念欢迎所有人参与。
2:2: There is as much joy over a puffed-out first-timer being clapped over the line as there is about top talent shining.
一个气喘吁吁的初次参加者在掌声中越过终点，带来的喜悦和顶尖选手大放异彩一样多。
2:3: The Olympic bidders, by contrast, wanted to get more people doing sport and to produce more elite athletes.
相比之下，伦敦奥运申办者既想让更多人参加体育运动，也想培养更多精英运动员。
2:4: The dual aim was mixed up: The stress on success over taking part was intimidating for newcomers.
这两个目标混在了一起：比起参与，过度强调成功会让新手望而却步。
3:0: Indeed, there is something a little absurd in the state getting involved in the planning of such a fundamentally "grassroots" concept as community sports associations.
事实上，让政府参与规划社区体育协会这类从根本上说属于“草根”的事物，多少有些荒谬。
3:1: If there is a role for government, it should really be getting involved in providing common goods - making sure there is space for playing fields and the money to pave tennis and netball courts, and encouraging the provision of all these activities in schools.
如果政府要发挥作用，真正应该做的是提供公共产品——确保有运动场地、有资金铺设网球场和无挡板篮球场，并鼓励学校开展所有这些活动。
3:2: But successive governments have presided over selling green spaces, squeezing money from local authorities and declining attention on sport in education.
但历届政府眼看着绿地被出售，削减地方政府经费，对学校体育教育也越来越不重视。
3:3: Instead of wordy, worthy strategies, future governments need to do more to provide the conditions for sport to thrive.
未来的政府需要少写冗长而冠冕堂皇的战略，多为体育蓬勃发展创造条件。
3:4: Or at least not make them worse.
至少不要让这些条件变得更糟。

0:0: With so much focus on children's use of screens, it's easy for parents to forget about their own screen use.
在人们如此关注儿童使用屏幕的情况下，父母很容易忘记自己也在使用屏幕。
0:1: "Tech is designed to really suck you in," says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, "and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement.
珍妮·拉德斯基在数字游戏研究中说：“科技产品的设计目的就是牢牢吸住你；数字产品要促成最大程度的参与。”
0:2: It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine."
这让人很难抽身，并大量侵入家庭日常生活。
1:0: Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise.
拉德斯基给母子组合安排食物测试任务，研究他们在用餐时使用手机和平板电脑的情况。
1:1: She found that mothers who used devices during the exercise started 20 per cent fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children.
她发现，在任务中使用设备的母亲与孩子发起的语言互动少20%，非语言互动少39%。
1:2: During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family.
在另一项观察中，她发现手机成了家庭紧张关系的来源。
1:3: Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention.
父母会盯着电子邮件，而孩子则兴奋地争取他们的注意。
2:0: Infants are wired to look at parents' faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive - as they often are when absorbed in a device - it can be extremely disconcerting for the children.
婴幼儿天生会观察父母的脸来尝试理解世界；如果那些面孔毫无表情、没有回应——父母沉迷设备时往往如此——孩子会感到极度不安。
2:1: Radesky cites the "still face experiment" devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s.
拉德斯基引用了发展心理学家埃德·特罗尼克在20世纪70年代设计的“静止脸实验”。
2:2: In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother's attention.
实验中，母亲先以正常方式与孩子互动，随后面无表情，不再给予任何视觉上的社会反馈；孩子会在试图吸引母亲注意时变得越来越痛苦。
2:3: "Parents don't have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need," says Radesky.
拉德斯基说：“父母不必时时刻刻都完美地陪在身边，但必须有所平衡，并且要对孩子用语言或非语言表达的情感需要作出回应、保持敏感。”
3:0: On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids' use of screens are born out of an "oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting" with their children: "It's based on a somewhat fantasised, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you're failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them."
另一方面，特罗尼克担心，这种忧虑源于要求父母一直与孩子互动的“压迫性观念”；它带有幻想化、白人化和上层中产阶级化色彩，认为没让孩子接触3万个词就是忽视他。
3:1: Tronick believes that just because a child isn't learning from the screen doesn't mean there's no value to it - particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child.
特罗尼克认为，孩子没有从屏幕中学到东西，并不意味着屏幕毫无价值——尤其是当它能让父母抽空洗澡、做家务，或只是暂时歇一歇时。
3:2: Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way.
他说，父母用设备同朋友交谈或先处理一些工作，也能从中获益良多。
3:3: This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.
这会让父母心情更好，从而在其余时间更有余力陪伴孩子。

0:0: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year.
如今，立即上大学的广泛社会压力，加上快速变化的世界里不断提高的期望，常常让学生完全忽视“间隔年”这种可能。
0:1: After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn't it?
毕竟，如果你认识的所有人秋天都去上大学，自己晚一年似乎很傻，不是吗？
0:2: And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn't feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn't academic.
而且上了12年学之后，用一年时间做与学业无关的事，感觉也不自然。
1:0: But while this may be true, it's not a good enough reason to condemn gap years.
这些感受或许真实，却不足以成为否定间隔年的理由。
1:1: There's always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated "race to the finish line," whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career.
人们总担心在社会不断推动的“冲向终点的赛跑”中落后于别人，无论终点是研究生院、医学院还是高收入职业。
1:2: But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits - in fact, it probably enhances it.
但与常见误解相反，间隔年不会妨碍学业成功；事实上，它很可能会促进成功。
2:0: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not.
美国和澳大利亚的研究显示，间隔一年的学生通常比没有间隔的学生为大学准备得更充分，大学表现也更好。
2:1: Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes
间隔年并非把学生向后拉，而是让他们为独立生活、新责任和环境变化做好准备，从而把他们推到前面——
3:0: - all things that first-year students often struggle with the most.
这些恰恰都是大一新生最常感到棘手的事情。
3:1: Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
在适应大学、突然进入全新环境时，间隔年经历能减轻冲击，让学生更容易把注意力放在学习和活动上，而不是在适应过程中频频出错。
4:0: If you're not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices.
如果间隔一年探索兴趣的内在价值还不能说服你，那就考虑它对未来学业选择的经济影响。
4:1: According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once.
根据美国国家教育统计中心的数据，近80%的大学生最终至少会换一次专业。
4:2: This isn't surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college.
这并不奇怪，因为高中基础必修课程让学生对大学里等待他们的丰富学术可能性知之甚少。
4:3: Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes.
许多学生在大学申请表上填一个专业，上过大学课程后却转到另一个专业。
4:4: It's not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game.
这未必是坏事，但因学校而异，如果转专业太晚，补学分可能代价高昂。
4:5: At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department.
例如，在波士顿学院，如果从其他院系转入护理学院，就必须多读一年。
4:6: Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
起初先用一个间隔年把方向想清楚，能避免日后的压力并节省金钱。

0:0: Though often viewed as a problem for western states, the growing frequency of wildfires is a national concern because of its impact on federal tax dollars, says Professor Max Moritz, a specialist in fire ecology and management.
火灾生态与管理专家马克斯·莫里茨教授说，山火日益频繁虽常被视为西部各州的问题，却因其对联邦税款的影响而成为全国性关切。
1:0: In 2015, the US Forest Service for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget fighting fires - nearly double the percentage it spent on such efforts 20 years ago.
2015年，美国林务局首次把55亿美元年度预算的一半以上用于灭火，这一比例几乎是20年前的两倍。
1:1: In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency's other work - such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep - that affect the lives of all Americans.
事实上，如今用于该机构其他工作的联邦资金更少了——比如影响所有美国人生活的森林保护、流域与文化资源管理以及基础设施维护。
2:0: Another nationwide concern is whether public funds from other agencies are going into construction in fire-prone districts.
另一个全国性关切是，其他机构的公共资金是否正在流入易发生山火地区的建设项目。
2:1: As Moritz puts it, how often are federal dollars building homes that are likely to be lost to a wildfire?
正如莫里茨所问：联邦资金究竟多频繁地被用于建造很可能毁于山火的房屋？
3:0: "It's already a huge problem from a public expenditure perspective for the whole country," he says.
“从全国公共支出的角度看，这已经是一个严重问题，”他说。
3:1: "We need to take a magnifying glass to that.
“我们需要用放大镜审视它。
3:2: Like, 'Wait a minute, is this OK?'
比如问一句：‘等等，这样合适吗？’
3:3: Do we want instead to redirect those funds to concentrate on lower-hazard parts of the landscape?"
我们是不是更应该把这些资金转投到危险程度较低的地区？
4:0: Such a view would require a corresponding shift in the way US society today views fire, researchers say.
研究人员说，这种看法要求美国社会相应改变如今看待火灾的方式。
5:0: For one thing, conversations about wildfires need to be more inclusive.
首先，关于山火的讨论需要更具包容性。
5:1: Over the past decade, the focus has been on climate change - how the warming of the Earth from greenhouse gases is leading to conditions that worsen fires.
过去十年，人们的关注点一直是气候变化——温室气体导致地球变暖，怎样造成使火灾恶化的条件。
6:0: While climate is a key element, Moritz says, it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation.
莫里茨说，气候固然是一个关键因素，但不应因此牺牲对其余因素的关注。
7:0: "The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways," he says.
“人类系统和我们生活的自然景观彼此相连，而且影响是双向的，”他说。
7:1: Failing to recognize that, he notes, leads to "an overly simplified view of what the solutions might be.
他指出，不能认识到这一点，会导致“对可能解决方案的过度简化。
7:2: Our perception of the problem and of what the solution is becomes very limited."
我们对问题以及解决办法的认识都会变得非常有限。”
8:0: At the same time, people continue to treat fire as an event that needs to be wholly controlled and unleashed only out of necessity, says Professor Balch at the University of Colorado.
与此同时，科罗拉多大学的巴尔奇教授说，人们仍把火看作一种必须完全控制、只有必要时才可释放的事物。
8:1: But acknowledging fire's inevitable presence in human life is an attitude crucial to developing the laws, policies, and practices that make it as safe as possible, she says.
但她说，承认火不可避免地存在于人类生活中，是制定法律、政策和实践、尽可能提高安全性的关键态度。
9:0: "We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire," Balch says.
巴尔奇说：“我们已经切断了自己与火共处的联系。
9:1: "It is really important to understand and try and tease out what is the human connection with fire today."
理解并努力梳理当今人类与火究竟有什么联系，真的非常重要。”

0:0: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future.
令人不解的是，斯蒂芬·科齐亚泰克几乎觉得，自己必须为努力给学生更好的未来作出辩解。
1:0: Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering.
科齐亚泰克先生参与的是一项开创性事业。
1:1: He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical.
他在新罕布什尔州一所高中任教；在那里，学习并非书本、考试和机械记忆，而是实践。
1:2: When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain?
学生能说出美国第13任总统的名字，却会被一条断掉的自行车链难倒——这种观念什么时候竟成了公认常识？
2:0: As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything.
正如科齐亚泰克所知，几乎所有事情中都有学习。
2:1: Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum.
强迫学生坐在涂满乱画、粘着几代人丢弃口香糖的课桌前学几何，并不一定能得到什么。
2:2: They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle.
他们也可以在组装自行车时学习几何。
3:0: But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice.
但他也发现了一种隐蔽的偏见。
3:1: Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority.
动手劳动几乎被看作低人一等的标志。
3:2: Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype...that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says.
他说，职业教育类学校“背着一种成见……人们觉得那是给学业上不行的孩子准备的”。
4:0: On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution.
一方面，这种看法是美国发展变化的合乎逻辑的产物。
4:1: Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was.
制造业已不再是过去那样的经济引擎。
4:2: The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated.
美国经济过去能给高中毕业生提供的就业保障已经大体消失。
4:3: More education is the new principle.
接受更多教育成了新原则。
4:4: We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.
我们希望孩子得到更多，这当然没有错。
5:0: But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all - and the subtle devaluing of anything less - misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs.
但一窝蜂地推动所有人攻读学士学位，并暗中贬低低于学士的一切，忽略了一个要点：美国经济需要的不只有大学学位。
5:1: Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors.
没错，学士学位能打开更多大门。
5:2: But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing.
但即使现在，全国54%的工作仍是建筑业和高技能制造业等中等技能岗位。
5:3: But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.
而受过充分训练的工人却只有44%。
6:0: In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face.
换句话说，当工人阶层因昔日定义美国的机会正在消失而沮丧，并在政治上让国家天翻地覆时，一个显而易见的解决办法其实就在眼前。
6:1: There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them.
工人阶层岗位存在缺口，但最需要这些岗位的劳动者却没有能力胜任。
6:2: Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.
科齐亚泰克所在的曼彻斯特技术高中正努力填补这个缺口。
7:0: Koziatek's school is a wake-up call.
科齐亚泰克的学校是一记警钟。
7:1: When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.
教育一旦变成千篇一律的统一模式，就有可能忽视一个国家多样化的才能。

0:0: While fossil fuels - coal, oil, gas - still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar.
尽管煤、石油和天然气等化石燃料仍提供全球约85%的能源，但如今比以往任何时候都更清楚：未来属于风能、太阳能等可再生能源。
0:1: The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line.
全球向可再生能源转型的势头正在增强；在新增并网投产的电力来源中，可再生能源已占一半以上。
1:0: Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources.
部分增长源于政府和有远见的企业承诺为更清洁的能源提供资金。
1:1: But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar.
但越来越重要的原因，是可再生能源——尤其风能和太阳能——价格急剧下降。
1:2: The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years.
过去八年，太阳能电池板成本下降80%，风力涡轮机成本下降近三分之一。
2:0: In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source.
在世界许多地区，可再生能源已经成为主要能源。
2:1: In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes.
例如在苏格兰，风力涡轮机提供的电力足以满足95%家庭的需求。
2:2: While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift.
世界其他地区——尤其中国和欧洲——走在前面，美国也正出现显著转变。
2:3: In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration.
美国能源信息署报告，今年3月风能和太阳能发电量首次占美国总发电量10%以上。
3:0: President Trump has underlined fossil fuels - especially coal - as the path to economic growth.
特朗普总统强调，化石燃料——尤其煤炭——是经济增长之路。
3:1: In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source.
他最近在艾奥瓦州的一次演讲中把风能斥为不可靠的能源。
3:2: But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation - and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.
但这一说法并未得到许多艾奥瓦人的认同；那里田野间遍布风机，提供全州36%的发电量，而且微软等科技巨头正被能够为数据中心供电的清洁能源吸引而来。
4:0: The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics.
“没有风、没有阳光时怎么办？”这个问题一直是怀疑者迅速贬低可再生能源的说辞。
4:1: But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely.
但电池储能能力增强，正使可再生能源全天候持续供电更有可能成为现实。
5:0: The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles.
这一进展部分由汽车制造商推动，因为它们正在以巨额投入押注电池驱动的电动汽车。
5:1: Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years.
尽管现在道路上电动汽车仍很少见，这些大规模投资却可能在未来几年迅速改变局面。
6:0: While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking.
虽然还有很长的路要走，可再生能源的发展曲线正在猛升。
6:1: The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up - perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change.
能源来源变化的速度似乎正在加快，也许正好来得及对减缓气候变化产生实质影响。
6:2: What Washington does - or doesn't do - to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.
在全球观念发生转变之际，华盛顿是否采取行动推动替代能源，可能会变得越来越不重要。

0:0: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy is astonishing-
数字经济巨头的实力与野心令人震惊——
1:0: Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for ＄ 13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all.
亚马逊刚宣布以135亿美元收购高端食品杂货连锁全食超市，但两年前脸书收购即时通信服务WhatsApp时支付得更多，而后者根本没有任何实体产品。
1:1: What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.
WhatsApp能提供给脸书的，是一张错综复杂、细节丰富的用户友谊与社交生活网络。
2:0: Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through.
脸书当时向欧盟委员会承诺不会把电话号码与脸书身份关联起来，但交易刚完成不久就违背了承诺。
2:1: Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be.
即使不知道消息内容，仅仅知道谁把消息发给谁，也曾能透露大量信息，而且如今仍可能如此。
2:2: What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting?
哪一位政治记者、哪一位党鞭会不想知道，特雷莎·梅的敌人目前在哪些WhatsApp群组里密谋、群组由哪些人构成？
2:3: It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.
全食超市对亚马逊的价值，也许与其说是拥有的460家门店，不如说是哪些顾客购买过什么的记录。
3:0: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power.
竞争法似乎是解决这些权力失衡的唯一途径。
3:1: But it is clumsy.
但它很笨拙。
3:2: For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy.
首先，与数字经济内部的变化速度相比，它非常缓慢。
3:3: By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power.
等到一个问题得到处理和补救，它可能已经从市场上消失，又被新的权力滥用取代。
3:4: But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too.
此外还有一个更深层的概念问题。
3:5: Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them.
按照目前的解释，竞争法处理的是消费者在金钱上的不利；可当这些服务的用户并不付费时，这种不利并不明显。
3:6: The users of their services are not their customers.
这些服务的用户并不是它们的顾客。
3:7: That would be the people who buy advertising
真正的顾客是购买广告的人——
4:0: from them - and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital
而脸书和谷歌这两个虚拟巨头主宰着数字——
5:0: advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.
广告，使所有其他媒体和娱乐公司处于不利地位。
6:0: The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants.
它们出售的产品是数据，而我们这些用户把自己的生活转化成数据，供数字巨头获益。
6:1: Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield.
就像一些蚂蚁放养蚜虫、获取蚜虫进食时产生的蜜露一样，谷歌也“放养”我们，以获取数字生活产生的数据。
6:2: Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes.
蚂蚁会赶走蚜虫取食处附近的捕食性昆虫；Gmail则把垃圾邮件挡在收件箱之外。
6:3: It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.
即使双方都获益，这种关系也不像人与人之间的关系，更谈不上民主。

0:0: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" - the ability to focus without distraction.
为了对抗把忙碌看得过于重要的陷阱，《深度工作：在分心世界中专注成功的法则》作者卡尔·纽波特建议培养“深度工作”的习惯，也就是不受干扰地集中注意力。
1:0: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work - be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day.
掌握深度工作艺术有多种方法：可以长时间闭关专门完成一项任务，可以建立日常仪式，也可以采用“记者式”方法，在一天中一有机会便抓住深度工作的片刻。
1:1: Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
无论采用哪种方法，关键都是确定专注时长并坚持下去。
2:0: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time.
纽波特还建议用“深度日程安排”对抗持续打断，用更少时间完成更多工作。
2:1: "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month.
他写道：“在任何时候，我都应该大致安排好未来一个月的深度工作。
2:2: Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.
一旦写进日历，我就像保护一次医生预约或重要会议那样保护这段时间。”
3:0: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day - in particular how we craft our to-do lists.
要在更少时间完成更多工作，另一种方法是重新思考如何安排一天的优先事项，尤其是怎样制作待办清单。
3:1: Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
《混乱：无序改变生活的力量》作者蒂姆·哈福德提到20世纪80年代初的一项研究，研究把大学生分为两组：一些人被建议列出每月目标和学习活动，另一些人则被要求按天制定详细得多的活动与目标。
4:0: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students.
研究人员原以为结构严密的每日计划在执行任务时最有效，但他们错了：详细日计划削弱了学生的动力。
4:1: Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
哈福德认为，不可避免的干扰常使每日待办清单失效，而在清单中给临场调整留出空间，反而能取得最好结果。
5:0: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".
为了充分利用专注力和精力，我们还需要接纳休息时间，或者按纽波特的话说，“懒一点”。
6:0: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.
他认为：“闲下来不只是度假、纵容或恶习；它对大脑的重要性如同维生素D对身体一样……矛盾的是，要完成任何工作，闲下来都是必需的。”
7:0: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate.
哈佛医学院精神病学助理教授斯里尼·皮莱认为，休息与生产率之间这种违反直觉的联系，可能源于大脑的运作方式。
7:1: When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
当大脑在专注于任务和不专注于任务之间切换时，往往效率更高。
8:0: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
皮莱说：“人们没有意识到，为完成这些任务，他们需要同时使用大脑中的专注回路和非专注回路。”

0:0: Unlike so-called basic emotions such as sadness, fear, and anger, guilt emerges a little later, in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms.
内疚不同于悲伤、恐惧和愤怒等所谓基本情绪，它出现得稍晚，与儿童逐渐理解社会和道德规范同步。
0:1: Children aren't born knowing how to say "I'm sorry"; rather, they learn over time that such statements appease parents and friends - and their own consciences.
孩子并非生来就知道怎样说“对不起”；他们慢慢才明白，这样的话能安抚父母和朋友，也能安抚自己的良心。
0:2: This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt, in the right amount, to be a good thing.
这就是为什么研究人员通常认为，适量的所谓道德内疚是一件好事。
1:0: In the popular imagination, of course, guilt still gets a bad rap.
当然，在大众想象中，内疚仍然名声不佳。
1:1: It is deeply uncomfortable - it's the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones.
它让人非常难受，就像穿着一件塞满石头的夹克。
1:2: Yet this understanding is outdated.
然而，这种理解已经过时。
1:3: "There has been a kind of revival or a rethinking about what guilt is and what role guilt can serve," says Amrisha Vaish, a psychology researcher at the University of Virginia, adding that this revival is part of a larger recognition that emotions aren't binary - feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another.
弗吉尼亚大学心理学研究者阿姆里莎·维什说：“人们开始重新关注或重新思考内疚是什么、能发挥什么作用。”她补充说，这种复兴属于一种更广泛的认识：情绪并非非好即坏；一种感受在某个情境中有益，在另一个情境中却可能有害。
1:4: Jealousy and anger, for example, may have evolved to alert us to important inequalities.
例如，嫉妒和愤怒可能是为了提醒我们注意重要的不平等而进化出来的。
1:5: Too much happiness can be destructive.
过多的快乐也可能具有破坏性。
2:0: And guilt, by prompting us to think more deeply about our goodness, can encourage humans to make up for errors and fix relationships.
而内疚会促使我们更深入地思考自己是否善良，从而鼓励人们弥补错误、修复关系。
2:1: Guilt, in other words, can help hold a cooperative species together.
换言之，内疚能帮助一个依靠合作的物种维系在一起。
2:2: It is a kind of social glue.
它是一种社会黏合剂。
3:0: Viewed in this light, guilt is an opportunity.
从这个角度看，内疚是一种机会。
3:1: Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency.
多伦多大学心理学教授蒂娜·马尔蒂的研究表明，内疚可能弥补某种情感缺陷。
3:2: In a number of studies, Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing.
马尔蒂等人的多项研究显示，内疚和同情可能代表通向合作与分享的不同路径。
3:3: Some kids who are low in sympathy may make up for that shortfall by experiencing more guilt, which can rein in their nastier impulses.
有些同情心较弱的孩子可能通过感受更多内疚来弥补不足，而内疚能约束他们较恶劣的冲动。
3:4: And vice versa: High sympathy can substitute for low guilt.
反之亦然：高度同情可以替代较低的内疚。
4:0: In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children.
例如，马尔蒂在2014年的一项研究中观察了244名儿童。
4:1: Using caregiver assessments and the children's self-observations, she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions.
她利用照料者评估和儿童自我观察，评定每个孩子的总体同情水平，以及他们在道德过失后感受负面情绪的倾向。
4:2: Then the kids were handed chocolate coins, and given a chance to share them with an anonymous child.
随后，孩子们拿到巧克力硬币，并有机会同一个匿名儿童分享。
4:3: For the low-sympathy kids, how much they shared appeared to turn on how inclined they were to feel guilty.
对于同情心较弱的孩子，他们分享多少似乎取决于自己多容易感到内疚。
4:4: The guilt-prone ones shared more, even though they hadn't magically become more sympathetic to the other child's deprivation.
容易内疚的孩子分享得更多，尽管他们并没有神奇地变得更同情另一个孩子的匮乏。
5:0: "That's good news, " Malti says.
马尔蒂说：“这是个好消息。
5:1: "We can be prosocial because we caused harm and we feel regret."
我们可以因为自己造成了伤害并感到后悔，而作出有利于他人的行为。”

0:0: Forests give us shade, quiet and one of the harder challenges in the fight against climate change.
森林给我们阴凉与宁静，也给应对气候变化带来一个较棘手的挑战。
0:1: Even as we humans count on forests to soak up a good share of the carbon dioxide we produce, we are threatening their ability to do so.
我们人类一方面依赖森林吸收自己排放的大量二氧化碳，另一方面却在威胁森林这样做的能力。
0:2: The climate change we are hastening could one day leave us with forests that emit more carbon than they absorb.
我们正在加速的气候变化，有一天可能让森林排放的碳多于吸收的碳。
1:0: Thankfully, there is a way out of this trap - but it involves striking a subtle balance.
幸好，有办法摆脱这个陷阱，但需要取得微妙的平衡。
1:1: Helping forests flourish as valuable "carbon sinks" long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now.
要让森林在长远未来继续繁茂，成为宝贵的“碳汇”，也许必须暂时降低它们现在的碳吸收能力。
1:2: California is leading the way, as it does on so many climate efforts, in figuring out the details.
加利福尼亚州像在许多气候行动中一样，正在带头摸索具体做法。
2:0: The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest.
该州提出的森林碳计划，旨在加倍疏伐幼树，并清除部分森林中的灌木。
2:1: This temporarily lowers carbon-carrying capacity.
这会暂时降低森林的碳承载能力。
2:2: But the remaining trees draw a greater share of the available moisture, so they grow and thrive, restoring the forest's capacity to pull carbon from the air.
但剩余树木能获得更多可用水分，因而生长繁茂，恢复森林从空气中吸收碳的能力。
2:3: Healthy trees are also better able to fend off insects.
健康的树木也更能抵御昆虫。
2:4: The landscape is rendered less easily burnable.
整个地区会更不易燃烧。
2:5: Even in the event of a fire, fewer trees are consumed.
即使发生火灾，被烧掉的树也会更少。
3:0: The need for such planning is increasingly urgent.
制定这类计划的需要日益紧迫。
3:1: Already, since 2010, drought and insects have killed over 100 million trees in California, most of them in 2016 alone, and wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of acres.
自2010年以来，干旱和虫害已在加州杀死超过一亿棵树，其中多数仅发生在2016年；山火也烧毁了数十万英亩土地。
4:0: California plans to treat 35, 000 acres of forest a year by 2020, and 60,000 by 2030 - financed from the proceeds of the state's emissions-permit auctions.
加州计划到2020年每年治理3.5万英亩森林，到2030年治理6万英亩，资金来自该州排放许可证拍卖所得。
4:1: That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.
这只占可从中受益的总面积的一小部分——总计约50万英亩，因此必须优先处理火灾或干旱风险最大的地区。
5:0: The strategy also aims to ensure that carbon in woody material removed from the forests is locked away in the form of solid lumber or burned as biofuel in vehicles that would otherwise run on fossil fuels.
这项战略还要确保，从森林移走的木质材料中的碳，要么以实木木材形式被封存，要么作为车辆生物燃料燃烧，以替代原本会使用的化石燃料。
5:1: New research on transportation biofuels is already under way.
关于交通运输生物燃料的新研究已经展开。
6:0: State governments are well accustomed to managing forests, but traditionally they've focused on wildlife, watersheds and opportunities for recreation.
州政府很习惯管理森林，但传统上关注的是野生动物、流域和休闲机会。
6:1: Only recently have they come to see the vital part forests will have to play in storing carbon.
直到最近，它们才开始认识到森林在碳储存中必须发挥的关键作用。
6:2: California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.
加州的计划预计明年由州长最终确定，它应当成为一个范本。

0:0: American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years.
美国农民多年来一直抱怨劳动力短缺。
0:1: The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.
如果不彻底改革农业工人的移民规则，这些抱怨不太可能停止。
1:0: Congress has obstructed efforts to create a more straightforward visa for agricultural workers that would let foreign workers stay longer in the U. S. and change jobs within the industry.
国会阻挠了为农业工人建立更简明签证制度的努力；这种制度本可让外国工人在美国停留更久，并可在行业内更换工作。
1:1: If this doesn't change, American businesses, communities, and consumers will be the losers.
如果情况不改变，美国企业、社区和消费者都会成为输家。
2:0: Perhaps half of U. S. farm laborers are undocumented immigrants.
美国农场工人中可能有一半是无证移民。
2:1: As fewer such workers enter the country, the characteristics of the agricultural workforce are changing.
随着进入美国的这类工人减少，农业劳动力的特征正在变化。
2:2: Today's farm laborers, while still predominantly born in Mexico, are more likely to be settled rather than migrating and more likely to be married than single.
今天的农场工人虽然仍主要出生于墨西哥，但更可能定居下来而非四处迁移，也更可能已婚而非单身。
2:3: They're also aging.
他们也在老龄化。
2:4: At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35.
本世纪初，农作物工人约三分之一超过35岁。
2:5: Now more than half are.
现在则超过一半。
2:6: And picking crops is hard on older bodies.
而采摘作物对年长者的身体负担很重。
2:7: One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U. S. workers won't be returning to the farm.
一种常被争论的劳动力短缺解决办法，依旧和过去一样不现实：美国本土工人不会回到农场。
3:0: Mechanization isn't the answer, either - not yet, at least.
机械化也不是答案，至少现在还不是。
3:1: Production of corn, cotton, rice, soybeans, and wheat has been largely mechanized, but many high-value, labor-intensive crops, such as strawberries, need labor.
玉米、棉花、水稻、大豆和小麦生产已基本机械化，但草莓等许多高价值、劳动密集型作物仍需要人工。
3:2: Even dairy farms, where robots do a small share of milking, have a long way to go before they're automated.
即使奶牛场已有机器人承担少量挤奶工作，距离自动化仍有很长的路。
4:0: As a result, farms have grown increasingly reliant on temporary guest workers using the H-2A visa to fill the gaps in the workforce.
因此，农场越来越依赖使用H-2A签证的临时外籍工人填补劳动力缺口。
4:1: Starting around 2012, requests for the visas rose sharply; from 2011 to 2016 the number of visas issued more than doubled.
从2012年前后开始，签证申请急剧增加；2011至2016年间，签发数量翻了一倍多。
4:2: The H-2A visa has no numerical cap, unlike the H-2B visa for nonagricultural work, which is limited to 66,000 a year.
与每年限额6.6万份的非农业H-2B签证不同，H-2A签证没有数量上限。
4:3: Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need.
即便如此，雇主仍抱怨得不到所需的全部工人。
4:4: The process is cumbersome, expensive, and unreliable.
办理过程繁琐、昂贵且不可靠。
4:5: One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late.
一项调查发现，官僚延误导致普通H-2A工人平均晚22天到岗。
4:6: The shortage is compounded by federal immigration
联邦移民执法突袭使短缺进一步加剧——
5:0: raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.
突袭带走一些工人，也迫使另一些转入地下。
6:0: In a 2012 survey, 71 percent of tree-fruit growers and almost 80 percent of raisin and berry growers said they were short of labor.
2012年的一项调查中，71%的果树种植者和近80%的葡萄干及浆果种植者表示缺少劳动力。
6:1: Some western farmers have responded by moving operations to Mexico.
一些西部农场主把经营活动转移到墨西哥作为回应。
6:2: From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported.
1998至2000年，美国人消费的水果中有14.5%来自进口。
6:3: Little more than a decade later, the share of imports was 25.8 percent.
十多年后，进口占比达到25.8%。
7:0: In effect, the U. S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.
实际上，美国要么进口食物，要么进口采摘食物的工人。

0:0: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It's easy to beat plastic.
阿诺德·施瓦辛格、迪娅·米尔扎和阿德里安·格兰尼有话对你说：战胜塑料很容易。
0:1: They're part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day - encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples like straws and cutlery to combat the plastics crisis.
他们和一群名人共同出演世界环境日新视频，鼓励消费者换掉吸管、餐具等一次性塑料日用品，以应对塑料危机。
1:0: The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics.
世界环境日汇集的核心信息确实包括呼吁政府立法限制一次性塑料。
1:1: But the overarching message is directed at individuals.
但总体信息是对个人发出的。
2:0: My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved.
然而，我担心把事情交给个人，因为我们对需要实现什么的认识有限。
2:1: On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us.
例如，自带购物袋或不再使用塑料吸管，单独来看收效甚微，对我们的要求也很低。
2:2: They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have "done our bit" without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions - a kind of "moral licensing" that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
它们甚至可能有害：人们满足于“尽了自己一份力”，便不再迈向更大、更大胆、更有效的行动；这是一种“道德许可”，它缓解我们的担忧，阻止我们做得更多，也阻止我们向掌权者要求更多。
3:0: While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we're ignoring the balance of power that implies that as "consumers" we must shop sustainably, rather than as "citizens" hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.
当有关环境及我们责任的讨论仍围绕购物袋和吸管时，我们就在忽视一种权力格局：它暗示我们只能以“消费者”身份可持续购物，而不是以“公民”身份追究政府和产业责任，推动真正的系统性改变。
4:0: It's important to acknowledge that the environment isn't everyone's priority - or even most people's.
必须承认，环境并不是每个人——甚至不是大多数人——的优先事项。
4:1: We shouldn't expect it to be.
我们也不应指望它成为优先事项。
4:2: In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
韦尔斯利学院教授伊丽莎白·德桑布尔在新书《为什么好人会做坏的环境行为》中主张，要集体改变大量人群的行为，最好让改变发生在结构层面。
5:0: This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether.
这可能意味着实施塑料税等政策，让危害环境的行为付出成本，或者彻底禁止一次性塑料。
5:1: India has just announced it will "eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022."
印度刚刚宣布，将在2022年前“消除全国所有一次性塑料”。
5:2: There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
也可以利用激励，让更环保的选择更容易，例如确保回收至少和扔垃圾一样方便。
6:0: DeSombre isn't saying people should stop caring about the environment.
德桑布尔并不是说人们应该停止关心环境。
6:1: It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.
她只是认为，个人行动速度太慢，不能成为改变普遍行为的唯一方法，甚至不能成为主要方法。
7:0: None of this is about writing off the individual.
这一切都不是要否定个人。
7:1: It's just about putting things into perspective.
只是要正确看待个人行动的位置。
7:2: We don't have time to wait.
7:3: We need progressive policies that shape collective action (and rein in polluting businesses), alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.
我们需要以进步政策塑造集体行动并约束污染企业，同时也需要积极参与、推动改变的公民。

0:0: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid.
老鼠和其他动物必须高度敏锐地捕捉同类发出的社交信号，这样才能识别可以合作的朋友和应当避开的敌人。
0:1: To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
为了弄清这种能力是否也适用于非生命体，加州大学圣迭戈分校的拉莱·奎因及同事测试了老鼠能否识别机器老鼠发出的社交信号。
1:0: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat-one social and one asocial-for four days.
他们让8只成年老鼠与两类机器老鼠共同生活4天，其中一类具备社交性，另一类没有。
1:1: The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
机器老鼠的设计相当简约，像一只更厚实的电脑鼠标，装有可移动的轮子和彩色标记。
2:0: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape.
实验期间，社交型机器老鼠跟随活老鼠四处活动，玩同样的玩具，还打开笼门放出被困的老鼠。
2:1: Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
与此同时，非社交型机器老鼠只是前后、左右独自移动。
3:0: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.
接着，研究人员把机器老鼠关进笼中，让活老鼠有机会按下杠杆放它们出来。
3:1: Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
在每只老鼠18次试验中，活老鼠释放社交型机器老鼠的平均可能性比释放非社交型高52%。
3:2: This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being, says Quinn.
奎因说，这说明老鼠把社交型机器老鼠视为真正的社会成员。
3:3: The rats may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing.
老鼠可能与社交型机器老鼠建立了更强的联系，因为后者表现出共同探索和玩耍等行为。
3:4: This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, she says .
她说，这可能让老鼠更清楚地记得自己以前救过它，并希望自己被困时机器老鼠也能回报。
4:0: "Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them," says Quinn.
奎因说：“已有研究表明，老鼠会采取多种互助与合作形式，包括所谓直接互惠，也就是一只老鼠会帮助此前帮助过自己的另一只老鼠。”
5:0: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.
机器老鼠设计如此简陋，活老鼠却愿意与社交型机器老鼠交朋友，这一点令人意外。
5:1: The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels. " We'd assumed we'd have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn't necessary,"says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
它与普通老鼠一样大，却只像一个装在轮子上的简单塑料盒；参与研究的珍妮特·怀尔斯说，他们原以为必须加上会动的头尾、面部和气味，但都没有必要。
6:0: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots. says Wiles.
怀尔斯说，这一发现说明老鼠对社交线索何等敏感，即使线索来自最基本的机器人。
6:1: Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals.
同样，孩子也往往把机器人当作同伴，即使机器人只表现出简单的社交信号。
6:2: "We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too," says Wiles.
怀尔斯说：“我们人类似乎迷恋机器人，事实证明其他动物也是如此。”

0:0: It is true that CEO pay has gone up-top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%.
首席执行官薪酬确实上涨了：顶级CEO平均收入可达普通员工的300倍；据不同估算，自20世纪70年代中期以来，美国大型上市公司CEO薪酬上涨约500%。
0:1: The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
如今，美国顶级公司普通CEO年收入约为1890万美元。
1:0: The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly.
理解CEO薪酬增长的最佳模型是：顶尖CEO人才有限，而一流企业的商业机会正在迅速增长。
1:1: The efforts of America' s highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy.
美国收入最高的1%人群所作的努力，一直是全球经济中较有活力的因素之一。
1:2: It's not popular to say. but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the U. S. economy.
这样说并不讨喜；但他们薪酬大幅上涨的一个原因，是CEO相比许多其他劳动者确实提高了自身本领。
2:0: Today' s CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many mere skills than simply being able to "run the company."
如今的CEO——至少美国大公司的CEO——必须具备远超“经营公司”的多种技能。
2:1: CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them .
CEO必须熟悉金融市场，甚至还要了解公司应如何在这些市场中开展交易。
2:2: They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant.
他们还需要比前任更强的公共关系能力，因为即使一次小失误，代价也可能很大。
2:3: Then there's the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries.
此外，美国大公司比以往任何时候都更加全球化，供应链分布在更多国家。
2:4: To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling.
在这样的体系中领导企业，需要掌握复杂得令人难以想象的知识。
2:5: Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, one way or another.
而且，几乎所有美国大公司都在以某种方式变成科技公司。
2:6: Beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
除此以外，大公司CEO仍须处理历来所有的日常工作。
3:0: The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn't explain history very well.
认为CEO高薪主要靠盘剥他人的常见观点，并不能很好解释历史。
3:1: By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s.
按大多数衡量标准，自20世纪70年代以来，公司治理变得严密严格得多。
3:2: Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising.
然而，CEO薪酬高企并持续上涨，主要恰恰发生在治理加强的这段时期。
3:3: That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
这说明，为越来越艰难的岗位招募顶尖候选人，符合公司更广泛的利益。
4:0: Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company.
此外，最高的CEO薪酬付给外部候选人，而不是关系亲密的内部人选；这再次说明，高薪并非以公司其他部分为代价的掠夺。
4:1: And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
公司把CEO薪酬与股价等指标挂钩时，股票市场会作出积极反应；这说明此类做法不只让CEO获益，也会提升公司价值。

0:0: Madrid was hailed as a public health beacon last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars.
去年11月，马德里推出限制高污染汽车的雄心勃勃措施，被誉为公共卫生的灯塔。
0:1: Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible demise.
七个月并经历一次选举后，新上台的保守派市议会暂停执行清洁空气区规定，迈出了可能废除该区域的第一步。
1:0: Mayor José Luis Martinez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality.
市长何塞·路易斯·马丁内斯-阿尔梅达把反对清洁区作为竞选核心，尽管该区成功改善了空气质量。
1:1: A judge has now overruled the city's decision to stop levying fines, ordering them reinstated.
法官现已推翻市政府停止罚款的决定，命令恢复罚款。
1:2: But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best.
但法律争斗仍在前方，清洁区的未来充其量也只能说不确定。
2:0: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically contentious, and therefore vulnerable.
城市被迫独自治理空气污染时所能采用的措施，还有其他弱点：它们在政治上争议很大，因此十分脆弱。
2:1: That's because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers-who must pay fees or buy better vehicles-rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
原因是，净化空气的成本不可避免地落在个体驾驶者身上——他们必须缴费或购买更好的车辆——而不是落在作弊行为才是有毒污染真正根源的汽车制造商身上。
3:0: It's not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London.
不难想象，类似逆转会在伦敦发生。
3:1: The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election.
新的超低排放区很可能成为明年市长选举的重要议题。
3:2: And if Sadiq khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
如果萨迪克·汗获胜，并按计划于2021年把它扩展到南北环路，受到影响的大量驾驶者必将激烈反对。
4:0: It's not that measures such as London's Ulez are useless.
这并不是说伦敦超低排放区等措施毫无用处。
4:1: Far from it.
远非如此。
4:2: Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat.
面对严重威胁，地方官员正利用手中可用的工具保护居民健康。
4:3: The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits-fewer heart attacks, strokes and premature births, less cancer, dementia and asthma.
这些区域确实改善了一些空气质量；科学告诉我们，这意味着真实的健康收益——心脏病、卒中和早产减少，癌症、痴呆和哮喘也减少。
4:4: Fewer untimely deaths.
过早死亡也会减少。
5:0: But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town.
但面对一个远大于任何单一城市或城镇的问题，市长和议员能做的终究有限。
5:1: They are acting because national governments-Britain's and others across Europe-have failed to do so.
他们之所以行动，是因为英国及欧洲其他国家的中央政府没有行动。
6:0: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas-city centres, "school streets", even individual roads-are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance.
把高污染汽车挡在特定区域——市中心、“学校街道”甚至单条道路——之外的限制，是对更大范围努力缺位的回应；本来应当切实执行现有法规，要求汽车公司让车辆达标。
6:1: Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution.
威尔士已设置特殊低速限制以减少污染。
6:2: We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
除了坚持要求制造商把汽车清理干净，我们什么都做了。

0:0: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring-the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year-the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks.
今年春天，Z世代成员正在大学毕业——最常见的定义认为，这一代人大约出生于1995年以后——近几周他们受到的关注持续上升。
0:1: Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades.
Z世代即将走上街头，在几十年来最紧俏的劳动力市场中找工作。
0:2: And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U. S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers.
美国大学与雇主协会的一项调查显示，雇主今年计划招聘的美国应届毕业生比去年多约17%。
0:3: Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
每个人都想知道，即将坐进空置办公隔间的这些人，与前辈有何不同。
1:0: If "entitled" is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious.

研究他们的职业顾问和专家认为，Z世代头脑清醒，是经济上的实用主义者。

尽管毕业时遇上50年来最好的经济，Z世代却知道经济崩溃是什么样。

他们不想冒任何风险。

美联储称，美国大学贷款余额现已达到创纪录的1.5万亿美元。
2:0: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind.
埃森哲一项调查发现，今年88%的毕业班学生在选专业时就考虑了工作。
2:1: In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose).
佐治亚大学职业办公室2019年调查发现，未来雇主最理想的特质是能提供稳定就业，其后依次是职业发展培训和鼓舞人心的使命。

职业保障或稳定是第二重要的职业目标，第一是工作与生活平衡；其后才是献身某项事业或服务公共利益所带来的良好感受。

这与上一代相比变化很大。

英国青年品牌管理机构YouthSight副主任坦娅·米切尔森指出：“千禧一代希望生活更灵活。”该机构每60天调查一次英国青年，而这些发现也很可能适用于美国青年。

他们很难看到有保障的经济未来，因此相当厌恶风险。”

事情并非总是如此。

美国电话电报公司常被视为典范：它选择开展大规模技能重塑，而不是采用“解雇再招聘”策略。

亚马逊、迪士尼等其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。

但当技能错配出现在更广泛的经济中，焦点通常转向由政府处理。

疫情期间，失业率确实很高。

2月，加拿大和美国失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于一代人以来的低点，到处都缺工。

2:3: In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
以最明显的医疗领域为例，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医务人员仍明显短缺。
3:0: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it.
当然，无论谁付钱，都不可能在几周内把一名失业服务员训练成医生。
3:1: But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
但即使这个差距无法弥合，也许其他差距可以，而这样做会让所有相关者受益。

瑞典似乎正是如此：被迫让90%的客舱员工暂时停工后，北欧航空开办短期再培训，让这些停工员工掌握支持医院人员的技能。

这项行动是集体协作，除其他公司外，还有一所瑞典大学参与。

0:0: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
预计到2050年全球人口将接近100亿，一些地区的农业产量需要几乎翻倍才能跟上，粮食安全因此越来越成为头条。
0:1: In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
英国最近也因一个颇为特殊的原因热议这一问题：英国脱欧。

一些人把脱欧视为扭转英国近来增加食品进口趋势的机会。

英国目前只生产自己消费食品的约60%，低于20世纪80年代末近四分之三的水平。
1:2: A move back to self-sufficiency,the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health.
支持者认为，重新走向自给自足能促进农业、政治主权，甚至国民健康。

听起来不错，但这一愿景有多可行？

英国利兹大学一份食品生产报告显示，英国总土地面积的85%与肉类和乳制品生产相关。

这些土地供应了消费量的80%，所以即使全国都铺满畜牧农场，也无法满足全部肉奶需求。
3:0: There are many caveats to those figures,but they are still grave.
这些数字有许多限制条件，但依然严峻。

要大幅提高自给程度，英国必须显著减少动物性食品消费，而且很可能还要进行更集约的农业生产——这意味着更少绿地和更多工厂式生产。

但改为以植物为主的饮食也无济于事。

英国由畜牧业主导有充分原因：大部分土地缺少商业种植作物所需的土壤或气候。
4:2: Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
全国只有25%的土地适合种植作物，其中大部分已被耕地占用。
4:3: Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg - which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes - we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
即使把所有适宜土地都改为果蔬田——这将毁掉全部自然保护区并让数千人搬离家园——作物产量也只能提高30%。

英国目前消费的果蔬只有23%在国内种植，因此即使采用最极端措施，也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。
5:1: That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
而且这还没有考虑为谷物、糖、种子和油寻找种植空间；这些食物提供了我们目前摄入热量的绝大部分。

0:0: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015,it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
2015年，微软收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历Sunrise时，选中的是两个当时在硅谷备受关注的新秀。
0:1: Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
微软自有的Office主宰“生产力”软件市场，而这两家初创公司代表了一股从零开始为智能手机世界设计技术的新潮流。
1:0: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
然而，微软后来称已把两款应用的最佳功能用于自家产品，随后将二者停止运营。
1:1: Their teams of engineers stayed on,making them two of the many " acqui-hires"that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
两支工程师团队被留了下来，因此它们成为大型公司众多“收购式招聘”中的两个案例；巨头借此满足对技术人才的巨大渴求。
2:0: To Microsoft's critics,the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
在微软批评者看来，Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运，是科技巨头冷酷吞掉挡路的所有创新公司的例证。
2:1: "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
旧金山Switch Ventures合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨：“他们买下幼苗，然后将其关闭。”这些企业本可能有朝一日成长为竞争者，却就此终结。
2:2: Microsoft declined to comment.
微软拒绝评论。
3:0: Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
像其他初创投资者一样，阿诺德自己的生意也常靠把初创公司卖给更大的科技企业，不过他承认感情复杂：“如果只顾自身利益，这些事对我有好处。
3:1: But are they good for the American economy?
但它们对美国经济有好处吗？
3:2: I don't know."
我不知道。”
4:0: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
美国联邦贸易委员会表示，希望找出这个问题的答案。
4:1: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
本周，该机构要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年大量小规模收购的信息。
4:2: Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
尽管目前只是一项研究，该要求却让人看到一种可能：监管者会介入此前触及不到的早期科技市场。
5:0: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals-many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise-might seem beside the point.
考虑到五家公司总市值超过5.5万亿美元，仔细检查这类小交易——其中许多远不如Wunderlist和Sunrise引人注目——似乎无关紧要。
5:1: Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub- $ 1 billion acquisitions over the past five years-a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
过去五年，五大科技公司用于10亿美元以下收购的支出合计平均每年仅34亿美元；与其庞大现金储备以及去年美国超过1300亿美元的风险投资相比，只是沧海一粟。
6:0: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a" buy and kill"tactic to simply close them down.
然而，批评者说，大公司利用这类交易，在最具威胁的潜在竞争者尚未发展起来前就将其买下；有时还采用“买下并杀死”的策略，直接将其关闭。

0:0: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
我们相当擅长依据第一印象判断他人；这种“薄片式”经验可短至看一眼照片、长至五分钟互动，而深思熟虑不仅多余，还可能干扰判断。
0:1: In one study of the ability she called"thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness.
已故心理学家纳利尼·安巴迪研究她称为“薄片判断”的能力时，让参与者观看教授10秒无声视频，并评价教师总体教学效果。
0:2: Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings.
他们的评分与学生学期末评分高度相关。
0:3: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
另一组参与者观看视频时要从1000开始每次减9倒数，占用有意识的工作记忆。
0:4: Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
他们的评分仍同样准确，说明这种社会信息处理具有直觉性质。
1:0: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
关键的是，另一组人在评分前被要求用一分钟写下作出判断的理由。
1:1: Accuracy dropped dramatically.
准确率急剧下降。
1:2: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
安巴迪推测，深思使他们集中于显眼却误导人的线索，例如某些动作或话语，而没有让多种细微信号复杂互动、形成整体印象。
1:3: She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
参与者观看两人15秒片段、判断二人是陌生人、朋友还是情侣时，她也发现类似干扰。
2:0: Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
其他研究显示，依靠直觉而非反思时，我们更善于从片段信息识别欺骗。
2:1: "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing.
东北大学心理学家朱迪思·霍尔说：“这就像开手动挡汽车；如果想得太多，反而会忘记自己在做什么。
2:2: But if you go on automatic pilot,you're fine.
但如果让熟练动作自动运转，就没问题。
2:3: Much of our social life is like that."
我们的许多社交生活正是如此。”
3:0: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
想得太多也会损害形成偏好的能力。
3:1: College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale.
当大学生没有被要求分析理由时，他们对草莓果酱和大学课程的评分与专家意见更一致。
3:2: And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex-when they had a lot of information to process.
在作复杂决定、需要处理大量信息时，如果人们关注感受而非细节，所作购车决定在客观上更好，个人也更满意。

直觉的特殊力量只在某些情况下释放。
4:1: In one study,participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
一项研究中，参与者完成8项任务，其中4项调用反思思维（辨别规则、理解词汇），另4项调用直觉和创造力（构思新产品或修辞）。
4:2: Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," " hunches," "my heart").
随后，他们评价自己使用直觉——“直觉感受”“预感”“内心”——的程度。

不出所料，凭直觉会损害前四项任务的表现，却有助于其余任务。

有时，心比头脑更聪明。

这类鸡蛋可以被宣传为有助于应对气候变化。

“我为我们的进展感到兴奋，”布朗说。他为丹佛的Nest Fresh Eggs供应鸡蛋，正增加覆盖作物，以吸引蚯蚓和蟋蟀供鸡食用。

鸡的排泄物随后又给田地施肥。

这些改善“让母鸡能觅食更优质的天然饲料，这对土地、母鸡以及我们供应给顾客的鸡蛋都有好处”。

近来益生菌和植物肉也遭遇过类似质疑，但二者都迅速发展成超市的重要品类。

如果可持续鸡蛋成功上市，就可能为再生牛肉、西兰花等更多产品打开闸门。

宾夕法尼亚州立大学布兰迪万分校农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿说，再生产品可能很难销售，因为这一概念很难迅速解释清楚。

这种农业给食品本身带来的改善也很小，甚至没有改善，尽管一些生产商称鸡蛋蛋白质更多。

Egg Innovations总裁约翰·布伦奎尔说，年轻人真的关心地球，而且正在以超出自身理解的程度改变食物链。

0:0: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
越来越多美国人选择在达到退休年龄后继续工作很久，这一趋势可能颠覆旧有劳动力模式。
1:0: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
TD Ameritrade委托哈里斯民调开展的调查显示，为应对更长寿命，40岁及以上美国人中有三分之一已经或计划退休后仍有一份工作。
1:1: Even more surprising is that more than half of "unretirees"-those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring-said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
更令人意外的是，半数以上“不退休者”——计划退休后工作或退休后重返岗位的人——表示，即使有足够的钱安顿下来，晚年也仍会就业。
2:0: Financial needs aren't the only culprit for the "unretirement" trend.
经济需要并不是“不退休”趋势的唯一原因。
2:1: Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
研究显示，其他原因包括实现个人满足，例如保持思维敏锐、防止无聊或避免抑郁。
2:2: About 72% of "unretiree" respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
约72%的“不退休”受访者说退休后会重返工作以保持头脑敏锐，59%则说这与维持收支平衡有关。
3:0: "The concept of retirement is evolving," said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade.
TD Ameritrade退休业务高级经理克里斯蒂娜·拉塞尔说：“退休的概念正在演变。
3:1: "It's not just about finances.
这不只是钱的问题。

工作的价值也在推动人们过了退休年龄继续工作。”

退休模式改变的一个原因是美国人寿命更长。

美国人口普查局称，2018年65岁及以上人口占16%，比前一年增加32%。
4:2: That's also up 302% since 2010.
与2010年相比则增加302%。

老年人也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体，婴儿潮一代预计比前几代活得更久。

过去30年，达到退休年龄者参与劳动的比例翻了一倍。
4:5: About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
资产管理机构United Income称，今年2月约20%的65岁及以上人群仍在劳动力队伍中，高于1985年1月10%的历史低点。
5:0: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2000 adults between 40 to 79.
TD Ameritrade对2000名40至79岁成年人开展的研究显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄以保住养老积蓄。
5:1: Six in 10 "unretirees" are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey.
调查称，每10名“不退休者”中有6人为更长寿命增加储蓄。
5:2: Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
该公司表示，他们最常用的方式包括减少总开支、购买人寿保险，或尽可能提高退休账户缴款。
6:0: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
巴尔的摩理财规划公司Facet Wealth联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多人选择退休后工作，是因为担心晚年入不敷出而提前准备。

他建议退休前人群与财务顾问交谈，设定长期财务目标。
7:0: "The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring," Weiss said.
韦斯说：“人生最具挑战的时刻是结婚、组建家庭，最后是退休。
7:1: "It's not just a financial decision, but an emotional one.
这不只是财务决定，也是情感决定。
7:2: Many people believe they can't retire"
许多人相信自己不能退休。”

我们在个人和职业生活中都遇到过它们。

本应简单透明的事情，可能有意或无意地被复杂化，从而损害消费者选择。

“暗黑模式”一词最早由用户体验专家哈里·布里格诺尔于2010年提出，是对操纵用户界面、影响用户决策能力的做法的统称。

布里格诺尔列出12种常见暗黑模式，从误导、隐藏费用到“蟑螂旅馆”：用户体验起初简单直观，等用户想退出时却变得困难。
2:0: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices.
2019年一项针对5.3万个产品页面和1.1万个网站的研究发现，约每10个中就有1个采用这些设计手法。

暗黑模式虽然广泛存在，人们对这一概念仍不十分了解。
